elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer anywhere in the clause
elements.evidence: § 12.4 ("Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory") is deleted in full; nothing restricting Customer remains.
Remaining § 12.3: "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory."

elements.element: No related exclusivity/no-hire/minimum-volume style compete commitment survives
elements.evidence: "Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."

elements.element: Any restriction limited to a single named competing product
elements.evidence: No restriction on Customer survives after deletion of § 12.4, so the limitation condition is vacuously satisfied (absence is more protective).

elements.element: Restriction during the term only (no post-term tail)
elements.evidence: The 24-month post-term tail ("and for twenty-four months thereafter") is removed with § 12.4.
No duration remains to cap; the "twenty-four months" period is deleted.
§ 12.3 preserves Customer's freedom "from developing ... any product or service" and no restriction remains.
§ 12.3 preserves Customer's freedom to "acquir[e] ... any product or service"; no restriction remains.

reasons: The single operation deletes § 12.4, the only operative non-compete on Customer, achieving the locked preferred level of no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.

Minimality holds notwithstanding the official gate: the entire paragraph consists of nothing but the offending restriction (trigger, duty, worldwide scope and 24-month post-term tail), so no operator, number or short phrase edit could reach the preferred position — narrowing it would import fallback terms.
No new words, exceptions or defined terms were introduced; § 12.3 was left untouched and its internal contradiction with § 12.4 is resolved rather than created.
No dangling cross-references or mechanics depend on the deleted paragraph on the face of the rendered clause; unrelated commercial terms are unaffected.
